correctness.rationale: All reduced cographs through eleven vertices are generated once using canonical alternating cotrees and all integer partitions of the leaf counts. Two separately coded 1-WL refinement routines agree on all 21101 objects. Exactly two size-11 representatives have four strict splits; they are complements. Independently, the explicit decomposition W=((P3+K1) join 2K1) disjoint ((K2+K1) join K2) gives class trace 1,3,5,6,7 by direct neighbor-color counts. Complementation preserves each split. The C2 rank interpretation follows by the standard induction on counted neighbor types. Critical computations are supplied as local reproducible code and full census, not just logs.

value.rationale: Quantifier rank of unary C2 types/1-WL refinement rounds is a natural descriptive-complexity parameter. Cographs are the canonical P4-free, modularly decomposable graph family; the first occurrence of four strict rounds has a sharply determined order and exactly two complementary witnesses. The connected witness has diameter two yet takes four rounds, showing that very small diameter and trivial modular decomposition do not by themselves force immediate counting-type stabilization. The exact finite cutoff and unique obstruction are useful boundary data for the unresolved higher-order cograph depth function; neither an arbitrary slice nor a sample of unrelated graphs.
